_provenance: Fitted on the open FPL dataset, seasons 2016/17 to 2024/25. 2025/26 is held out entirely and untouched, per the calibration protocol. Nothing in this file is hand-picked.

promotion_factor._definition: points per 90 of promoted-club players in their first PL season, divided by players at the SIX WEAKEST ESTABLISHED clubs that season
promotion_factor._why_this_definition: The previous factor divided by the whole league (0.7511 overall, DEF 0.6336). That double-counts: the fixture multiplier and clean-sheet layer already know a promoted club is weak, so applying the whole-league ratio on top penalised them twice. Measured against clubs of similar strength, the promotion effect proper is much gentler and forwards show essentially none.

history_blend_k._fitted_on: 2017/18-2024/25 walk-forward, 59546 player-gameweeks with a prior-season rate
history_blend_k._definition: weight on the current season is m/(m+k) where m is minutes played so far
history_blend_k._method: grid search minimising mean absolute error on predicted gameweek points
history_blend_k._note: The optimum is flat between 900 and 1200 minutes (MAE 1.2442 at both). 1000 is taken as the midpoint. Roughly eleven full matches before this season outweighs last season.
history_blend_k._ranking_check: Refitted on rank correlation across eight training transitions (2017/18 to 2024/25): ranking improves monotonically with k up to 1200, mean +0.1455. This agrees with the average-error fit, so 1000 stands. A single held-out season suggested dropping the prior-season layer; the training refit contradicted it, so the layer stays.

starts_proxy._note: Seasons before 2022/23 have no starts column. minutes >= 60 is used as the proxy and agrees with the real starts flag in 94.7% of 83835 rows where both exist (2022/23-2024/25).

minutes_scaling._definition: A per-90 rate is multiplied by expected ninetieths of a match: p_start x exp_min_start + p_cameo x exp_min_cameo, capped at 90 minutes.
minutes_scaling._measured_on: Held-out 2025/26, predictions made before kickoff so minutes were not known.
minutes_scaling._note: Largest single improvement available from components that already existed. Applied in lib/solver/score.mjs and only when a forecast exists.

rate_shrinkage._definition: A prior-season per-90 rate is pulled toward the position mean by n/(n+S), where n is the player's prior-season ninety-minute blocks and S is fitted below. Small samples move a long way toward the mean.
rate_shrinkage._method: Grid search minimising mean absolute error on predicted gameweek points.
rate_shrinkage._note: S=24 is a heavy shrink: a player with 24 full matches last season gets half his own rate and half the position mean. Reliability on the held-out season independently shows the raw rates are over-spread, under-predicting low scorers and over-predicting high ones, which is the same conclusion.

reliability_2025_26._definition: Mean predicted against mean actual by quintile of prediction, held-out season, expected minutes applied.
reliability_2025_26._reading: Negative in the bottom three quintiles and positive in the top means the spread is too wide. Shrinking the rates toward the position mean is the correction, which is what rate_shrinkage does.

dixon_coles_rho._status: FITTED AND REJECTED ON EVIDENCE. Kept at zero because the correction does not describe this data.
dixon_coles_rho._fitted_on: 1900 Premier League matches, 2020/21 to 2024/25, scorelines reconstructed from goals conceded, which is authoritative because it already includes own goals.
dixon_coles_rho._method: Maximum likelihood over the full independent-Poisson likelihood multiplied by the Dixon-Coles tau correction.
dixon_coles_rho._result: rho = +0.02, log-likelihood -5327.94 against -5328.04 at rho = 0. The surface is flat, so the correction earns nothing.
dixon_coles_rho._why_it_fails: Dixon-Coles assumes 0-0 and 1-1 are both more common than independence predicts, and tau moves them in the same direction. Observed: 272 goalless draws against 229 expected, but only 200 one-all draws against 255 expected. The two cells move in opposite directions, which no single rho can represent.
dixon_coles_rho._conclusion: Not a failed fit. A measured finding that this correction is the wrong shape for this league over this period. Any future attempt should model the two cells separately rather than through one parameter.

home_advantage_measured._units: goals per match, home mean minus away mean
home_advantage_measured._why_not: EXCLUSIONS 12.8: home advantage is already priced into bookmaker odds, and a layer on top double-counts it. Recorded as a diagnostic only. Nothing reads this value.

team_strength_ratings._what: Poisson attack and defence ratings per club, fitted iteratively with a home factor, intended as the odds-free fallback for team goal expectation.
team_strength_ratings._fitted_on: 1140 matches, 2022/23 and 2023/24. Tested out of sample on 2024/25.

_result.change: -2.4% worse than a flat league mean

team_strength_ratings._why_cut: DECISIONS 9.10: any layer that fails to beat the simpler version out of sample gets cut, no exceptions. Prior-season strength does not transfer, because squads change between seasons.
team_strength_ratings._note: Fitted values looked entirely plausible (Arsenal and Liverpool strongest defences, home factor 1.25). Plausibility is not evidence, which is exactly why the gate exists.

minutes_blend_apps._definition: Weight on the current season for the start-rate blend: w = appearances / (appearances + W).
minutes_blend_apps._method: Grid search minimising Brier score on P(start).
minutes_blend_apps._improvement: 5.3% better Brier than the hand-picked 8. Start rate moves far faster than points rate: one appearance already outweighs last season, where points needed roughly eleven matches.

p60_given_start._definition: Probability of reaching sixty minutes given an expected start, split on expected minutes when starting.
p60_given_start._method: Threshold grid search; within each bucket the optimal constant is the observed rate.
p60_given_start._note: The hand-picked values were badly wrong, 0.86 against a true 0.55. They assumed a likely starter almost always reaches sixty minutes; in fact substitutions make it close to a coin flip.
